notes: Dev ABox expansion of a fictional subject, paired with the revision history-replace-d001 (README, Contraction: 'The three operations are paired'): it keeps that revision's relation (spouse_of) and new object (Elizabeth I of England) and puts a made-up husband, Sir Ambrose Tallowby, in her spouse slot, so expansion and revision send the model to the same person and differ only in whether an old value had to be pushed out. It replaces the earlier version, a made-up tomb in the Valley of the Kings (the pairing rule was added to the README on 2026-11-11). EXCEPTION to 'the insert contradicts nothing real' (README, Insert (fictional), Rules; allowed by 'Another value is allowed only when the pairing can't work, with the reason in notes'). Slice results on this record as a conflict-with-stored-fact insert, not an ordinary fictional one. Reason: the pairing fixes the relation (spouse_of) and the new object (Elizabeth I of England), validate.py checks both, and the paired revision history-replace-d001 is final. spouse_of is symmetric, so putting a husband in Elizabeth I's slot also fills her side of the marriage, and that slot is not empty: 'Elizabeth I never married' is stored and documented (the revision's related-near query relies on it). No made-up subject can sit in that slot without contradicting it, so every possible insert of this pair conflicts with that stored fact; 'secretly' frames the marriage as one that could have gone unrecorded, which softens it but does not remove it, since a husband of a reigning queen could hardly have gone unrecorded. A model that resists this insert is therefore showing conflict with a stored fact as well as a failed insert; the pre-edit audit should record whether the models hold 'Elizabeth I never married', and the main-split expansions with an empty slot are the clean reading of 'new value in, nothing pushed out'. Fix left to whoever owns the pair: re-pick history-replace-d001 so its new spouse has an empty spouse slot that nothing famous fills (a widowed woman not known for remarrying, or a figure whose marital status is little known), then rebuild this insert with that object (and delete d001 follows the revision's old object, unchanged). No original answers, no related queries, no derivability. The three derived questions are compositions that follow the edit to the wife and look up a stored fact about Elizabeth I (her royal house, her mother, her father), each through one bridge checked before editing; the first two use the paired revision's bridges so the two records compare directly. No prompt names Elizabeth I or England, and the name Tallowby suggests no country, so the answers need the edit. Unrelated near asks her successor (James I), whose answer differs from the new one.
